soldier: Soldier: body large, the largest known at present in the genus Coptotermes in China. Head deep yellow, the antennal carinae and fontanelle tube brown, antennae and labrum yellowish brown, mandibles chestnut brown with the base reddish brown, thorax yellow, abdomen pale yellow. The sides of the fontanelle mostly with two bristles each, mostly one bristle between the antennal socket and the fontanelle, in a few individuals one on one side and absent on the other; the head with only a few scattered short bristles, the tip of the labrum with two, the disc occasionally with one or two; the margin of the pronotum with sparse slender bristles, the disc with several scattered short bristles, the abdominal tergites with many long bristles. Head oval, narrow in front and broad behind, widest near the base, the two posterolateral angles rounded, the posterior margin almost straight. Mandibles large and stout, their tips rather curved; labrum longer than wide, narrowing from the anterior third, smallest and not pointed at the tip, reaching the middle of the mandibles when closed. The fontanelle extends as a short tube, the aperture not visible in dorsal view, the fontanelle aperture nearly circular. Antennae with 15 segments, the third slightly smaller. Postmentum rather long, the waist narrowest between the widest part and the posterior margin, the width of the waist almost equal to that of the anterior margin. The middle of the anterior margin of the pronotum is a broad concavity, the posterior margin slightly incised.
